title: Pitch and Volume
seo_title: Year 4 Science: Pitch and Volume Worksheets (High and Low, Loud and Quiet)
standard_text: Find patterns between the pitch of a sound and features of the object that produced it. Find patterns between the volume of a sound and the strength of the vibrations that produced it. Recognise that sounds get fainter as the distance from the sound source increases.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 science worksheets on pitch and volume: high and low notes, loud and quiet sounds, distance, decibels, and bottle and sound meter investigations. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Pitch: high or low. Volume: loud or quiet.
key_sub: Shorter and tighter means higher; bigger vibrations mean louder.
body_html:
How to think about it

Pitch is how high or low a sound is; volume is how loud it is.

  • Shorter, tighter, thinner and smaller objects vibrate faster and make higher notes.
  • Bigger vibrations make louder sounds. Sounds get fainter the further you are from them.
  • Volume is measured in decibels (dB); sounds above about 85 dB can damage hearing over time.
Example

Tighten a guitar string. Pitch?

Tighter vibrates faster

Answer: higher

Example

Hit a drum harder. Change?

Bigger vibrations

Answer: louder, not higher

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a longer string gives a higher note.
  • Mixing up pitch and volume.
  • Thinking sounds get louder as you move away.

faq.q: What is the difference between pitch and volume?
faq.a: Pitch is how high or low a sound is. Volume is how loud or quiet it is. A sound can be high and quiet, or low and loud.

faq.q: How can you change the pitch of a string?
faq.a: Make it shorter, tighter or thinner for a higher note, or longer, looser or thicker for a lower note.

faq.q: Why do sounds get quieter further away?
faq.a: The vibrations spread out as they travel, so less of the sound's energy reaches your ears.

items.q: Which usually makes a higher note: a small drum or a big drum?
items.e: Smaller vibrates faster.

items.q: What happens to the pitch when a bigger drum is hit?
items.e: Shorter, tighter, thinner and smaller things vibrate faster and make higher notes.

items.q: What happens to the pitch when you blow across a bottle with more water in it (less air)?
items.e: Shorter, tighter, thinner and smaller things vibrate faster and make higher notes.

items.q: Why do ear defenders protect hearing?
c: They absorb sound so less reaches the ears.
items.e: Muffling sound.

items.q: How could you make a higher note on a xylophone?
items.e: Pitch depends on the size and tightness of what vibrates; volume depends on how big the vibrations are.
